chunks: Al-Riḍā عليه السلام was asked about the skins of properly slaughtered foxes, and he said: “Do not pray in them.”
16 — Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from a man:

He asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about praying in fox skins, and he forbade prayer in them and in what is adjacent to them. I did not know which of the two cloths was meant: the one that sticks to the fur or the one that sticks to the skin. So he عليه السلام wrote in his own hand: “The one that sticks to the skin.” And Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام mentioned that he was asked about this issue, and he said: “Do not pray in what is above it, nor in what is beneath it.”
17 — As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about praying in fox skins, and he said: “If they are properly slaughtered, then there is no problem.” So it is possible that what was meant is that there is no problem with it if it is on something like a cap or something similar from that by which prayer is not complete. And what clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:
18 — Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, who said:

I wrote to Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام asking him: May one pray in a cap upon which there is fur from an animal whose meat is not eaten, or in a silk belt, or in a belt made from rabbit fur? He wrote: “Prayer is not lawful in pure silk, but if the fur is from a properly slaughtered animal, prayer in it is permissible, if Allah, Most High, wills.” It is also possible that what is meant by ‘in’ in the report is ‘upon,’ as though he عليه السلام said: there is no problem in standing upon it during prayer. We have already explained, from the narrations, what necessitates the prohibition of prayer in them, in what is sufficient, if Allah, Most High, wills. And that is also reinforced by what he narrated:

key_terms.جُلُودِ ٱلثَّعَالِبِ: fox skins, the material under legal discussion for use in prayer
key_terms.ذَكِيَّةً: properly slaughtered according to Islamic law
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem, indicating permissibility in context
key_terms.لَا تُصَلِّ فِيهَا: do not pray in them, an explicit prohibition
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.ٱلْحَرِيرِ ٱلْمَحْضِ: pure silk, a material in which prayer is stated to be unlawful
key_terms.ٱلْوَبَرُ: fur or soft hair attached to the animal skin

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat in fox skins or clothing made from the fur of animals whose meat is not eaten?
ai.summary: These reports discuss the legal ruling on praying in garments made from fox skins and similar materials. The text presents narrations that prohibit prayer in fox skins, then addresses another report that appears permissive by restricting it to items such as caps or cases where the material is not used as a full prayer garment.
